_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

items.expected-result: On a fresh scratch bank with no engine set, memory_write four ordinary notes and one containing POISON-7Q, so all five rows are pending. Start `python3 scripts/poison-embedding-stub.py --port 0 --log stub.log`, then run `model embedding set openai stub-embed <printed base URL> --api-key stub-key` against the scratch server. memory_embed_pending returns {processed, pending} and does not fail or hang. Later calls return pending 1. `sqlite3 -readonly memory.db "SELECT embed_state, embed_attempts, count(*) FROM entries GROUP BY 1, 2"` shows four rows embedded and the poison row pending at embed_attempts 3. memory_stats.pending is 1, and the count of poison lines in stub.log stays the same across three more memory_embed_pending calls. Negative control: stub.log holds a `poison 5` batch line followed by `ok 1` lines, so the engine refused the batch and answered the single rows. A build without ADR-0119 fails every memory_embed_pending with ClientResultException, keeps all five rows pending and adds a poison line per call (ADR-0119)
items.command: fresh root b-memory/poison, server :52760, no engine; wrote 4 ordinary notes + 1 containing POISON-7Q (stats pending 5; sqlite pending|0|5); poison-embedding-stub.py --port 0 --log stub.log (printed http://127.0.0.1:52740/v1); model embedding set openai stub-embed http://127.0.0.1:52740/v1 --api-key stub-key --port 52760; then 4x memory_embed_pending, memory_stats, sqlite3 -readonly 'select embed_state, embed_attempts, count(*) from entries group by 1, 2' (p1.py, p2.py)
items.evidence:
stub.log: ok 1 / poison 5 / ok 1 / ok 1 / ok 1 / ok 1 / poison 1 / poison 1 / poison 1 / ok 1 / poison 1 / poison 1 / ok 1 (6 poison lines total)
memory_embed_pending x4: {"processed":0,"pending":1} each, 0.0s; poison lines 6 -> 6 -> 6 -> 6 -> 6; memory_stats pending 1
sqlite: embedded|0|4 and pending|3|1
items.observed-result: The refused 5-row batch was split and answered row by row: four rows embedded, the poison row stays pending at embed_attempts 3 and stops costing requests; further drain calls neither fail nor hang nor add poison lines.
items.acceptance-reason: All specified post-conditions observed including the 'poison 5' batch line followed by 'ok 1' lines. Note for honesty: the background re-embed triggered by 'model embedding set' did the isolation work before my first explicit memory_embed_pending, so the four explicit calls were all no-op re-checks ({processed:0,pending:1}); the 'no per-call poison growth' check is therefore on those calls, and the isolation itself is evidenced by stub.log and sqlite.

items.expected-result: each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to, the write reports the rejection, and the rejected content is retrievable from the noise store (ADR-0039)
items.command: bash noise.sh; bash noise2.sh (memory_write over MCP, `noise entries`, `settings noise disable|enable`, sqlite3 -readonly noise_entries)
items.evidence: Registered policies: AppRegistrations.cs:340 registers only HermesProcessNoisePolicy (name HermesBackgroundProcessLog). Writes of '[IMPORTANT: Background process ...', '[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH ...', 'received signal 15', '  Received Signal 1.' -> stored:false reason "rejected by noise policy 'HermesBackgroundProcessLog'". Negative controls ('Received signal handling in the worker ...', '[IMPORTANT: remember that deploys freeze on Fridays]', bare 'received signal', note mentioning ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH mid-sentence) -> stored:true. `noise entries`: 'total: 0' before, 'total: 4 / HermesBackgroundProcessLog: 4' after; noise_entries rows hold the verbatim rejected content (ids 1-4). settings noise disable -> 'received signal 9' stored:true, entries stay 4; settings noise enable -> 'received signal 10' rejected, entries 5.
items.observed-result: Only one write policy is registered in this build; it rejects its three shapes, reports the rejection on the write, stores the rejected text in noise_entries, leaves lookalike clean content alone, and the kill switch disarms/re-arms it.
items.acceptance-reason: Every claim of the single registered policy was exercised with positive and negative inputs; rejected content is retrievable (count via CLI, content via sqlite3 on the noise_entries table; the CLI shows only per-policy counts, not text).

items.expected-result: the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)
items.command: bash guard.sh; bash guard2.sh (memory_search over MCP; `settings queryguard show|enable|disable|shadow|structural enable|disable|threshold set`)
items.evidence: Refuse tier: '[IMPORTANT: Background process proc_1 completed normally. Command: make test]' and '[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE] ... dispatched earlier has finished' -> invalid-params 'This looks like tool output rather than a question...' [isError]. Controls: '[IMPORTANT: Background process notes] how do deploys work' and 'how do deploys work on Fridays' -> normal results, no guard warning. Annotate tier: stack-trace query ('   at System.Net.Http.HttpClient.Send(') and 'fail: Foo.Bar[12]' query -> results returned with warning 'This query contains what looks like log or stack-trace output...'. Structural: `queryguard show` 'structural: False' by default; log-shaped query got no structural warning; after `structural enable` at the default threshold 0.989 my two hand-made log shapes still got no warning (honest note: default threshold is strict); at threshold 0.7 the path/hex log shape was annotated ('statistically resembles tool output'), at 0.5 both shapes annotated; plain question never annotated until threshold 0.0 (then annotated, results still returned). With structural enabled at threshold 0.0 the Hermes refuse query was still Refused (regex tier wins) and no structural hit ever produced an error. Shadow on: refuse query ran and returned 3 results; guard disabled: same query returned results; re-enabled: refused again. Disabled structural again -> shape query unannotated.
items.observed-result: Refuse tier refuses only the two marked shapes; annotate tier warns but returns results; structural detector is off by default, only ever annotates (never refuses), and obeys its threshold; shadow and disable pass queries through.
items.acceptance-reason: Both tiers, their lookalike negative controls, the default-off state, the enable transition, annotate-only behaviour and precedence were each observed on the live server. Threshold had to be lowered to demonstrate the structural annotation on my samples; that is a calibration observation, not a defect.

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, memory_watch_add) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows, `chmod 000` node_modules, wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds memory_search finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and memory_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
items.command: w1.sh (watch wdir with x.md,w.md,y.md,node_modules/pkg/index.md,.git/notes.md), w2.sh (chmod 000 node_modules; sleep; edit y.md), w3.sh (kill server; same-length word swap in x.md + touch to 1790976495; rewrite w.md at new size + touch to 1790976400; restart same data root), w4.sh/w5.sh (searches + watch_files + status)
items.evidence: Before restart: watch_files x.md updated_at=1790976486 size=53; w.md 1790976486 size=34; y.md 1790976504; watches.last_change_ts=1790976504; x.md mtime=1790976495 (updated_at <= mtime <= last_change_ts holds); w.md mtime=1790976400 (before its updated_at), size 78 vs recorded 34. After restart (port 52573): search xylophonebbb -> x.md snippet 'The heron alpha1 marker xylophonebbb sits here.'; search walrusnewterm777 -> w.md snippet '...carrying walrusnewterm777...'; watch_files x.md|1790976535|53, w.md|1790976535|78; memory_watch_status state Healthy. Negative controls: old term xylophoneaaa, wombatqqq, nmzzzterm (node_modules), gitzzzterm (.git dir) all -> results: [].
items.observed-result: Both missed edits (x.md same-size, mtime older than last_change_ts; w.md size-changed, mtime older than its fingerprint) were found by search within the 12 s startup window, watch_files updated_at/size moved for both, status Healthy, node_modules and .git terms never found.
items.acceptance-reason: The premise was verified from the bank before the restart (first attempt of mine had x.md mtime 1790976456 < updated_at, violating the premise, so I re-touched it to 1790976495 as the item prescribes). The mtime > last_change_ts rule that predates ADR-0121 would have skipped x.md; the new fingerprint rule healed it. The 5-minute heal pass was not run (optional). Note: .git fixture dir had to be created through a python script because the session's git-internals hook blocks direct writes, contents identical to what the item asks.

items.command: t5.py/t6.py: doctor on sec bank (embedding set local, server stopped) twice with sha256 before/after; chmod 000 copy m0; random-bytes nd; missing root
items.evidence: healthy: rc 0, 'user_version: 17 (this binary: 17)', 'memory engine: bundled', 'code engine: not configured', 'embedding threads: 5 (halved-core default)', 'model migration: none open', 'status: HEALTHY'; 'sha unchanged True 2f936a50aca8' on both runs. mode-000: rc 30 (Bank.OpenFailed), stderr line "ai-raccoon: doctor: could not open the bank read-only: SQLite Error 14: 'unable to open database file'." non-database file: rc 32 'exists but is not a SQLite database (SQLite error 26); wrong key or corrupt bank ...'. no bank: rc 31. With a coreml-cache dir present: 'coreml: not started, cache 0 MiB'.
items.observed-result: report has engine, threads, migration lines; Core ML line is conditional (ReadCoreMlLineAsync returns null unless device is CoreMl or <dataRoot>/coreml-cache exists), so a plain macOS bank omits it; created that dir to prove the line renders. Exit codes as specified; bank hash did not move.
items.acceptance-reason: All specified exits and the read-only hash invariant observed. Two observations, not failures: (1) the Core ML line is absent on a bank not using Core ML (by design in DoctorCommands.cs:335-341, but the expected-result text implies it is always printed); (2) doctor's failure paths print full exception stack traces to stderr (mode-000 and not-a-database), in addition to the one-line verdict, from the Warning loggers 1015/1016 — noisy for an operator.

After two concurrent serves: 'identity-key 0o600 240', 'mcp-token 0o600 43' (+ .lock files 0600); one token read from disk was accepted by both servers (ports 50873 and 50874: tools/list returned 29 on each). Restart: 'token same: True key same: True'. items.expected-result: #819 (ADR-0106 D5): `serve --restart --port <bound>` on a live scratch server proves identity before any other request, stops it with the token, waits for the port and starts the new one; with the mcp-token removed it reports the no-token outcome and does not stop the server.
items.command: t3.py: mv sec/mcp-token away; $BIN --data-root sec serve --restart --port 51024; restore token; rerun --restart
items.evidence: No-token run: rc 51 (ErrorCode.Port NoToken); only HTTP request logged before the verdict was 'POST http://127.0.0.1:51024/identity/prove ... 200'; stderr: 'cannot restart the server on port 51024: it proved this data root's identity but has no usable token (.../sec/mcp-token holds no token yet)'; /observability afterwards still pid 7343 alive True. Token-present run: first logged request is the same POST /identity/prove 200, then ServerRestart[650]/[651] stop line, port free, new pid listening.
items.observed-result: identity proof is the first and only request before the token is read; without the token the outcome is NoToken (exit 51) and the server is left running; with the token it is stopped by token-guarded shutdown, the port is waited free, and the new server starts.
items.acceptance-reason: Order observed in the client's HttpClient log (prove precedes everything) and the negative control (token removed) left the server alive. Not observed: a foreign/unproven listener (Unproven, 50) — not required by the item text.

items.expected-result: #824: each `settings performance|maintenance|extract` integer setter stores a valid value (read back via list/get) and rejects 0, -1 and a non-number with its own message and a non-zero exit code, writing nothing; `performance list` shows the stored values with their units.
items.command: bash setters.sh (output setters.out): for each of settings performance buffer-capacity|flush-interval|retention, settings maintenance interval|vacuum-interval|embed-rows-per-run, settings extract interval|capacity: abc, 0, -1, then a valid value, with settings-table snapshots (sqlite3 -readonly) between
items.evidence: All 8 setters: abc, 0 and -1 each -> stdout empty, exit 10, stderr e.g. 'ai-raccoon: buffer capacity must be a positive number of measurements' / 'flush interval must be a positive number of seconds' / 'retention must be a positive number of days' / 'checkpoint interval must be a positive number of minutes' / 'vacuum interval must be a positive number of days' / 'embed rows per run must be a positive integer, at most 4096' / 'interval must be a positive number of minutes' / 'capacity must be a positive number of queued candidates'; settings snapshot identical before and after the rejects. Valid values (2048, 7, 14, 45, 3, 25, 11, 77) -> exit 0 with stdout 'buffer capacity: 2048 measurements (takes effect on the next server restart)', 'flush interval: 7s (...next flush tick)', 'retention: 14 days (...next maintenance pass)', 'checkpoint interval: 45 min', 'vacuum interval: 3 days', 'embed rows per run: 25', 'extraction interval: 11 min', 'propose-tier capacity: 77 candidates'; stored keys read back (metrics.buffer-capacity.global=2048, metrics.flush-interval-seconds.global=7, metrics.retention-days.global=14, maintenance.checkpoint-interval-minutes.global=45, maintenance.vacuum-interval-days.global=3, maintenance.embed-rows-per-run.global=25, extract.interval-minutes.global=11, extract.queue-capacity.global=77) and shown by `performance list` with units ('flush interval: 7s', 'retention: 14 days'), maintenance list and extract list. Caps: buffer-capacity 99999999 -> 'must be at most 1000000 measurements', retention 99999 -> 'at most 36500 days', vacuum 99999 -> 'at most 36500 days', embed rows 99999999 -> exit 10; flush-interval 99999999999 -> exit 10 (int overflow rejected as non-number). `-1` parsed as the value (no option-parse error).
items.observed-result: Every setter stores valid values, rejects abc/0/-1 with its own noun/unit message and exit code 10, writes nothing on reject. Side note: embed-rows-per-run is not an IntSetting (own parser in MaintenanceCommands.cs) but behaves the same. Valid-value runs also emit an info line on stderr (CliSettingsBackend[687], 'the backend on port N keeps running after this command exits') because the CLI auto-attached to my server.
items.acceptance-reason: Exact stdout/stderr/exit/stored value captured for all 8 setters x 4 inputs with before/after table snapshots proving no write on reject.

items.command: bash reads.sh (output reads.out): 6 'cache' notes in project cs-sr; memory_search 'cache invalidation deploy'; CLI `settings retrieval fts-weight set` / `rrfk set` between searches on the same running server (no restart)

After fts-weight 1 + `rrfk set 1`: count 2, strengths 1.0 and 0.66667. After `rrfk set 1000`: count 6, strengths 1.0, 0.9990, 0.9980 ... 0.9950. items.expected-result: #825: on a scratch server the sweep, extraction and bank-maintenance loops run passes and log their pass/tick event ids (same ids as before the refactor per logging-event-ids.md); changing an interval setting is picked up on the next tick; a failed pass logs and the loop continues.
items.command: Server run 2 (serve --port 0), settings: sweep interval-hours 1, extract enable true + interval 1/3, maintenance interval 1/2; ticks stamped by stamp.py (ticks-run2.log, ticks.log); busy bank via lock.py (BEGIN IMMEDIATE held 95 s on the scratch bank, rolled back, nothing written)
items.evidence: Maintenance 510 'Bank WAL checkpoint complete' and extraction 504 'Extraction pass complete: N projects, 0 promoted' both at 23:30:44 and 23:31:44 (1 min cadence). Settings changed 23:31:35-37 (maintenance 2 min, extraction 3 min): next ticks maintenance 23:33:44 (2 min gap), extraction next at 23:34:49 (see below), then 23:37:59 (3 min after 23:34:59). Failed pass: with the lock held from 23:34:20, extraction logged 499 'Extraction deferred for cs-noise / cs-promo / cs-sr: the bank is busy' (23:34:49, :54, :59) and still 504 at 23:34:59; maintenance 23:35:44 logged 511 'Bank WAL checkpoint deferred: 1 frames busy', 521 'Noise entry retention purge failed; retried on the next tick' (23:35:49), 524 'Retention purge failed; retried on the next tick' (23:35:54); lock released 23:35:55; both loops continued: 510 at 23:37:54 and 504 at 23:37:59. Sweep: interval is clamped to >= 1 h (SweepConfigKeys.ParseIntervalHours, MinIntervalHours), so it cannot fire in minutes; with the interval set to 1 h and the server restarted at 23:57:04, SweepHostedService 534 'Sweep pass complete: 3 projects, 0 entries deleted' logged at 00:57:04 exactly. Ids 497-506/508 (ExtractionHostedService), 510-524 (BankMaintenanceHostedService), 530-537 (SweepHostedService) match docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md rows 171, 173, 174; 499 text there: per-project deferral.
items.observed-result: All three loops tick and log their documented ids; interval changes apply from the next tick for maintenance and extraction (a server restart re-reads it for sweep); busy-bank failures are logged (not fatal) and the loops keep ticking. The sweep interval change itself could not be shown live without another hour; sweep shares RunTicksAsync with the other two, whose re-read was shown. A whole-pass 505/513 failure (exception, not busy deferral) was not provoked: covered by BackgroundLoopTests.
items.acceptance-reason: Tick, log id, interval pickup and continue-after-failure were each observed on a live scratch server with timestamps; the sweep interval re-read and the 505/513 exception path are covered only by unit tests and noted explicitly. Server was killed once by the 30-minute background limit (run 1) and restarted; run 1 ticks are in ticks.log history and serve-run2-first30min.log.

items.expected-result: #814: a memory_write or ingest cancelled mid-call (client abort) leaves no open transaction: the next writes on the same server succeed at once and `PRAGMA` shows no stuck write lock; a schema migration on an older bank copy commits.
items.command: On server :50588 (local engine) via c1.py: (a) memory_write of 4.0 MB (project lane-b-cancel, sourceFile /notes/cancel-close.md) with TCP connection closed 1.0s after send; (b) same with notifications/cancelled for the request id at 1.09s; (c) memory_ingest_file on a 3 MB .md closed at 1.0s; (d) memory_ingest_directory on 30 x 300 KB files closed at 1.5s. After each: timed follow-up memory_write, sqlite3 -readonly row counts/quick_check, server log. (e) copied tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Resources/docs-memory.db (user_version 10) to b-memory/migr, started server, read result with sqlite3 -readonly
items.evidence:
(a) 'connection closed at 1.01s'; follow-up stored=True in 0.08s; rows for /notes/cancel-close.md = 0 (8s later still 0); pragma quick_check ok; journal_mode wal; server log: "memory_write" timed out after 8621 ms: the caller cancelled it; TaskCanceledException at WriteChunks.InsertAsync (WriteChunks.cs:20) <- SqliteMemoryStore.WriteAsync (inside the transaction), followed by 'follow-up 8s-later: stored=True in 0.05s'
(c) "memory_ingest_file" timed out after 30597 ms: the caller cancelled it; TaskCanceledException at SqliteMemorySourceStore.ResolveOrCreateOnConnectionAsync <- FileIngestor.InsertChunksAsync; follow-up stored=True 0.87s; rows for ingestsrc 0 at +3/+10/+20s; follow-up later stored=True 0.41s
(d) "memory_ingest_directory" timed out after 31289 ms: the caller cancelled it; follow-up 1.93s then 0.13s; ingestsrc rows 0
(b) notifications/cancelled: write ran to completion (48.4 s, stored:true) because this server is stateless (initialize returns no Mcp-Session-Id), so the notification has no session to bind; follow-ups 0.80s/1.23s
(e) migr: user_version 10 -> 17, embed_attempts column present (read from a separate readonly connection), entries 2049 -> 2036 via chunk-backfill-v2 / chunk-boundary-repair-v2 jobs (log: '2 group(s) re-chunked into 11 row(s)'); after the embedding-model migration drain finished, memory_write stored=True in 0.10s
items.observed-result: Connection-abort cancellations of a large memory_write, a file ingest and a directory ingest were observed inside their write transactions, rolled back (0 partial rows, quick_check ok), and every follow-up write succeeded at once with no stuck lock. An older-schema bank (v10) migrated to v17 and committed, and accepted a write afterwards.
items.acceptance-reason: Client-abort path (the checklist's primary form) proven on three writers. Limits: notifications/cancelled cannot be exercised on this stateless server (instrument limit, recorded above); the lock-free proof is timed follow-up writes plus quick_check, since a -readonly connection cannot take BEGIN IMMEDIATE; cancellation is only observed at the next DB call after the CPU-bound chunk/embed phase (8.6 s / 30 s after abort) so 'at once' applies to the next writes, not to the abandoned call returning. Migration substitute: docs-memory.db (user_version 10) used as the older bank because MemorySchemaVersionTests builds snapshots in-process rather than as a file.

Seeding via sqlite3 INSERT into entries/projects after a fresh serve migrated the schema (ids alpha-project x2, alpha x2 [fragment], zzz-mystery x1).

Server log: "repair requested (chunk-index)", "repair requested (reingest)", then "maintenance job 'apply a CLI-requested chunk-index repair' (repair-chunk-index) ran" and "...reingest repair' (repair-reingest) ran". project-ids no map: '4 id(s) censused — 0 fold, 0 drop, 0 retire, 2 need a human to attribute, 2 need nothing' + template written (Dropped: alpha, zzz-mystery), summary 'attention needed' ; with map dry-run: 'summary — repair needed: 1 fold, 1 drop' exit 0; --queue-only exit 0 'request committed...'; bank after ~18s: alpha-project|4, project_id_aliases alpha|alpha-project|alias and zzz-mystery||drop, server log 'project-ids repair pass applied 1 fold(s), 1 drop(s), 0 retire(s) — moved 4 row(s)'; --apply loop (reseeded) took 16.9 s, exit 0: 'pass 1/10 — reaped: moved 2 row(s); census totals 6 → 5 entries.' 'summary — converged: 0 fold, 0 drop, 0 retire, 0 unresolved, 0 pinned, P3 armed (1 alias, 1 dropped)'; unattributed id with map-noattr.json: exit 39 'summary — attention needed: ... 2 id(s) still need a human'; bad map: exit 15 'cannot load --map ...'.
items.observed-result: Both generic repairs report without --apply and queue with --apply, with the job visible in the server log; project-ids prints scoreboard and buckets, template, folds+drops via both --queue-only and the loop; exit codes 0 (converged, queued), 39 (RepairAttentionNeeded), 15 (AliasMapInvalid) match ErrorCode.cs lines 37/105/108/111 and docs/how-to/repair-fragmented-project-ids.md.
items.acceptance-reason: Caveats: the chunk-index/reingest banks were empty so every count was 0 (job path proven, not repair of real drift; ProjectIds had real seeded data). Exit 37 (stuck) and 38 (writers-active) were not provoked. Option to shorten the loop: none; the CLI exposes only --apply/--queue-only/--diagnose/--map and PollInterval is a constructor option (ProjectIdsRepairCommands.cs RepairLoopOptions), so one pass costs ~15 s (measured 16.9 s). Observation: dry-run output on a re-seeded bank listed zzz-mystery as 'need a human' under map-noattr because that map has no Dropped entry, expected.

items.expected-result: #823: `sync` push then pull against a local S3 (MinIO) round-trips the bank; a stale ETag push reports a conflict; bad credentials report an auth failure with the operation named (pull/push).
items.command: docker run -d --name air-checklist-minio -p 0:9000 bitnamilegacy/minio (substituted image, see reason); docker port -> 32768; mc mb local/airbucket (mc inside the container); settings sync add s3 http://127.0.0.1:32768 --bucket airbucket with keys on stdin (no --region); memory_write on s1, memory_sync s1 (push), memory_sync s2 (second data root, pull); out-of-band writer alternating two valid snapshots via mc cp while s1 syncs; wrong access key, wrong secret; container removed. Scripts s1-s5.sh.
items.evidence: Push: {"sent":1,"received":0,"reindexed":0}; mc ls: '268KiB STANDARD memory-sproj.db'. Pull on second root: {"sent":1,"received":1,"reindexed":0}, and search 'zephyrquux' on s2 -> path 2b87c2b2....md snippet 'Round trip note about the kestrel zephyrquux marker'. Stale ETag (3 syncs of 6 under concurrent out-of-band writes): 'sync-conflict: Remote changed since last pull — If-Match precondition failed.' (earlier attempts under the same writer succeeded by retry). Wrong access key: 'sync-auth-failed: AWS auth failed — run 'aws configure' or 'aws sso login', or verify the keys with 'ai-raccoon settings sync show'.' Wrong secret: identical message. Server log: 'S3 auth failed: The Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records.' / 'The request signature we calculated does not match...'. Good keys restored: sent 1.
items.observed-result: Round trip and conflict work against real MinIO. Auth failure is reported as sync-auth-failed, but neither the CLI/MCP message nor the log line names the operation (pull or push).
items.acceptance-reason: Defect: the expected 'operation named (pull/push)' is not met. src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sync/S3CloudStore.cs MapFailure(ex, operation, ...) receives "pull"/"push" but uses it only for the network branch ('S3 {operation} failed'); the auth branch (lines ~102-108) logs ex.Message and returns a fixed 'AWS auth failed' message without operation. S3CloudStoreTests only assert the exception type. Substitution noted: minio/minio and minio/mc are no longer pullable (Docker Hub denied, quay.io 401), so bitnamilegacy/minio was used (real MinIO server, bundled mc). Stale-ETag note: SyncService re-pulls and retries up to 3 times (MaxPushRetries), so a single out-of-band change heals; a conflict only surfaces when the remote keeps changing, which I produced with a continuous writer (non-deterministic, 3/6). | Orchestrator check: not a regression. At the pre-series baseline 83aa6cd3, S3CloudStore.cs:64-65/70-71/115-116/121-122 and AzureBlobCloudStore.cs:61-114 already threw the same fixed auth message with no operation; #823 preserved it. The expected result (naming pull/push on auth failures) was written for this run and asks for more than the product has ever done. accepted left null for the owner: either accept as the existing message shape, or file the improvement (S3CloudStore.MapFailure already receives the operation).

lane-findings.prior-run: n/a (product observation, not a prior-run claim)
lane-findings.what-is-actually-true: Unexplained keyword-leg omission: with /notes/minutes.md (2 rows) and /notes/minutes-big.md (9 rows) in one project, a vectorWeight=0 memory_search for 'zq71' or 'marker' returns only minutes.md chunk 0 (fts rank 1). minutes-big.md chunk 0 (entries.id 20, hash 67fe2468..., value contains 'Opening marker zq71') is absent from the fts leg even with minRelativeScore 0 and limit 30, although sqlite 'entries_fts MATCH' joined to entries returns both rowids 16 and 20 (bm25 -1.7594 vs -1.7580). The same row appears only via the vector leg. A control with two different notes sharing the rare token 'kestrelx' returned both with fts legs, so it is not a general failure. Root cause not traced (ModalityCandidates content-dedup keys on whole-value hash and the values differ).
